title: Resilience orchestration: SLO-aware retry budget, idempotency surface, and hedged-request SDK contract
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Problem: Different services and SDKs implement retries, timeouts, and hedging inconsistently. This has led to duplicate side-effects (no consistent idempotency contract), broken SLOs during regional failover, unbounded cost from naive hedged fanout, and confusion for product teams about safe retry semantics. Goal: define and implement a single SLO-aware retry/backoff surface + idempotency contract and hedged-request primitives across server libraries and SDKs; integrate with circuit breakers and load-shedding so customer-facing SLOs are preserved and costs bounded.
acceptance_criteria: Standardized HTTP/gRPC header contract published: X-Idempotency-Key semantics, scope (resource vs operation), deduplication window defaults, and TTLs documented
Hedged-request contract defined with explicit budget token semantics: maximum fanout, hedging delay heuristics, and SLO-credit consumption model documented
Client library (go/ts/py) implements unified resilience: RetryPolicy, HedgePolicy, Idempotency middleware, and CircuitBreaker hooks with feature flags
Server-side deduplication middleware in runtime accepts X-Idempotency-Key and provides deterministic 2xx/4xx/5xx mapping, with configurable dedup store TTL and observability metrics
SLO-aware retry governor implemented at routing layer: per-customer SLO-credit accounting that prevents retries/hedges from violating latency/error SLOs across regions
End-to-end integration tests and chaos tests covering single-region and multi-region failover are in CI and pass
Dashboards and alerts created: retry budget burn rate, hedged fanout rate, duplicate side-effect count, idempotency cache hit/miss, and circuit-breaker open rate
Migration plan and opt-in rollout documented with automatic fallback for non-compliant callers and a deprecation timeline for legacy headers

notes: Rationale for header choices: Use conventional header names so 3rd party integrators don't need translation layers. Include optional parameters in a structured, parseable token (semi-colon delimited).

Hedging defaults: Start with disabled hedging for write operations unless caller supplies explicit 'hedge-prefer' header. Read-heavy endpoints can enable conservative hedging by default with max fanout=2 and hedge-delay = 10% of SLO p50 latency.

Idempotency semantics: For non-idempotent write operations, server must either accept and deduplicate (if idempotency key supplied) or reject fast with 409 if required by operation contract. Default dedup-window = 5 minutes for write operations; configurable per-route.

SLO-credit model: Each request consumes tokens based on expected tail latency and historical variance. Retries and hedged replicas draw from same credit pool. If budget exhausted, client-side SDK must short-circuit and surface a retriable=false error to callers or fall back depending on route config.

Migration: Provide shim middleware that translates legacy retry headers to new contract, log warnings, and emit telemetry to track non-compliant callers. 8-week deprecation window after pilot completion.
